licensure.disciplinary_grounds.rationale: These nine buckets capture the dominant clusters across all states: fraudulent application/license-obtaining acts, competence/negligence failures, criminal history, code/statute violations, improper license lending or identity misuse, contract abandonment/fund diversion/payment failures, aiding or being unlicensed persons, substance/physical impairment, and procedural failures like supervision lapses, recordkeeping, insurance, and non-cooperation with boards.

profession_specific.license_tiers.rationale: The data naturally clusters into the classic trade-ladder tiers (apprentice, journeyman, master), a separate contractor/business-entity license, gas-fitter tracks that run parallel to the plumbing ladder in several states, limited-scope or specialty licenses (residential-only, restricted, drain cleaner, backflow, irrigation, etc.), and endorsements that attach to a base license (medical gas, fire sprinkler, water supply protection), covering all observed items without requiring a large catch-all.

profession_specific.journeyman_experienc.rationale: The items cluster around formal apprenticeship completions, hour-based supervised on-the-job experience, academic/trade-school credits, military service pathways, reciprocity from other states, standalone examination requirements, and catch-all board-determined equivalency provisions, which together cover every pathway in the dataset without significant overlap.
